overview: Quality Studio combines named review rules, repository policy and reproducible evidence. Reviewers explain a concrete problem; measurements help decide where to look. A score alone does not establish correctness.

principles.title: Actionable findings
principles.why: A finding should help someone reproduce and fix a problem, rather than record a reviewer preference.
principles.method: Describe the trigger, source location, affected behavior and a proportionate fix. Check edge cases, concurrent work and failure recovery; relate severity to the concrete impact.
principles.limits: Readability suggestions are advice unless they violate an agreed rule or cause a demonstrated maintenance problem. Missing context is uncertainty, not proof of a defect.

principles.title: Clear ownership and dependency direction
principles.why: Explicit boundaries make it easier to find a feature and understand which changes can affect it.
principles.method: Compare source placement and imports with the repository contract. Keep Angular feature code together and components focused; separate application responsibilities in .NET.
principles.limits: backend/<projects>, backend/tests and frontend/src are this repository’s convention. A directory named src is not inherently wrong, and a folder tree cannot prove component cohesion.

principles.title: Consistent and usable interfaces
principles.why: Shared controls and typography reduce visual drift and make similar actions behave consistently.
principles.method: Use the declared design tokens and native interaction semantics. Check keyboard access, loading/error states and the actual rendered UI; enforce the repository’s font and bundle budgets.
principles.limits: The local 11 px minimum catches an agreed floor, not complete readability or accessibility. Browser zoom, contrast, content length and interaction still need inspection.

principles.title: Bounded work and observable failure
principles.why: A change must stay understandable and responsive when data grows, requests race or dependencies fail.
principles.method: Review cancellation, cache keys, resource bounds and stale responses. Measure realistic scenarios and write tests that fail when externally visible behavior breaks.
principles.limits: A passing benchmark is evidence for its workload and machine. Coverage and a green test run do not establish that every important behavior was asserted.

metrics.title: Review coverage
metrics.formula: round(100 × files with review documents / reviewable files, 1)
metrics.why: Shows which reviewable files have recorded review evidence.
metrics.interpretation: An empty scope reports 0%. A file counts when it has a review document for any kind.
metrics.limits: A stale review still counts; this is not test coverage or proof that all review kinds are fresh.

metrics.title: Test line coverage
metrics.why: Shows which reported executable lines were reached by tests.
metrics.interpretation: Reads supported coverage reports; a reported XML line rate may provide a percentage without counts.
metrics.limits: Missing or invalid reports are unavailable, not 0%. Executed lines do not prove useful assertions, branch coverage or correct behavior.

metrics.title: Risk view score
metrics.formula: round(0.4 × (100 − code grade) + 0.4 × (100 − line coverage %) + 20 × changes / max(1, largest change count), 2)
metrics.why: Prioritizes files with weak recorded grades, less coverage and more recent changes.
metrics.interpretation: The churn window is the requested number of days (90 by default). A missing grade or coverage value leaves the score unknown.
metrics.limits: This is a prioritization heuristic, not a failure probability. Inspect review and coverage freshness before using the score.

metrics.title: Findings per KLOC
metrics.formula: round(1000 × unresolved findings in review documents / max(1, file lines), 2)
metrics.why: Normalizes the dashboard’s finding count by file size.
metrics.interpretation: Counts findings across recorded review kinds using the dashboard’s resolution filter.
metrics.limits: A small file can have high density. Findings depend on review scope, policy, recency and reviewer judgment; compare like-for-like.

metrics.title: Dashboard hotspot priority
metrics.why: Combines churn, finding density and recorded grade to order the dashboard’s review candidates.
metrics.interpretation: An unknown code grade uses 50 for this ranking; zero changes produce zero. This differs from the coverage-based Risk view.
metrics.limits: The fallback is an explicit ranking assumption, not an assigned grade. A low score does not imply safety or complete review coverage.

metrics.title: Recorded and effective review grade
metrics.formula: When E > 0: effective = min(security cap, clamp(roundAway(100 − (100 − base) × I / (I + E)), base, 100)). When E = 0: effective = base. Project summary: roundEven(mean(available recorded root scores per review kind)).
metrics.why: Explains both the recorded review assessment and the current triage-adjusted grade. A finding-status change can change the displayed effective score without another review.
metrics.interpretation: Base is the stored review score (0–100). I sums included finding weights: open and accepted. E sums excluded weights: waived, false-positive, resolved or actively suppressed. Weights are critical 16, high 8, medium 4, low 2, otherwise 1. roundAway rounds a midpoint away from zero; roundEven rounds a midpoint to the nearest even integer. For reviews with a security verdict, the cap is 79 for warn and 59 for block or unavailable; otherwise it is 100. The cap applies to the adjustment when E > 0. Observed example: three high findings with one marked false-positive leave I = 16 and E = 8; base 72 (C) becomes 81 (B), unless a security cap applies. Bands are A ≥ 90, B ≥ 80, C ≥ 70, D ≥ 60, otherwise F.
metrics.limits: The base is reviewer judgment. Triage can raise the effective grade without changing code or test coverage; excluded observations remain in the history. Project summaries average recorded root grades, not the effective grades of all files; missing scores are excluded. Inspect findings, policy, security signals and freshness alongside any grade.
